observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a bare engine block, apparently removed from a vehicle, sitting on a shop floor.
Visible parts: 4 ignition coil packs on top of a valve cover, intake manifold area, alternator, drive belt and pulleys, an oil filler cap labeled 'ENGINE OIL'.
A watermark reads 'POSTED ON JIJI / EMMY GOLD AUTO SPARE' - this is the seller's shop branding, not an engine marking.
No manufacturer logo, engine code, displacement marking, or VIN/parts plate is legible in either photo.
No wiring harness, ECU, intake/exhaust manifolds beyond what's shown, or starter motor are visible - engine may be partial.
No scale reference or background context (no car, no engine bay) to confirm vehicle fitment.

identity.kind: 4-cylinder petrol engine (bare, used, for Hyundai/Kia per seller)

claims.evidence: No logo, cast marking, or engine code is readable in photo 0 or photo 1; Hyundai and Kia share many engine platforms so visual confirmation requires a legible code or plate, which is absent.
Photo 0 shows 4 ignition coil packs in a row, consistent with an inline-4 configuration.

risks.risk: Exact engine code/displacement (e.g. 1.4L G4FA vs 1.6L G4FC vs 2.0L Theta) is unknown, and this drives most of the price difference within 'Hyundai/Kia 4-cylinder' engines.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the cast engine code on the block or the ID plate/sticker.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest common Hyundai/Kia 4-cylinder engine variant

risks.risk: Running condition (compression, oil leaks, internal wear, whether it starts) cannot be judged from static photos.
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine cranking/running with audible sound, or a compression test reading.

risks.risk: Completeness - engine may be missing starter, sensors, turbo (if applicable), or wiring harness needed for a swap.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set showing all sides including the back (bellhousing/flywheel) and underside (oil pan, starter mount).
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete, assuming missing ancillary parts

risks.risk: Mileage/usage history and reason for removal (accident, flood, mechanical failure) is unknown.
risks.proof: Seller-provided donor vehicle documents, mileage photo from odometer, or history of the part.

risks.risk: Visible residue/staining near the mount area in photo 1 could indicate an oil leak or gasket failure.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stained area and the oil pan gasket/rear main seal.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming leak repair is needed

proof_requests: Clear photo of the cast engine code or ID plate on the block (to confirm exact Hyundai/Kia model and displacement).
Video of the engine running or being cranked, with sound.
Photos of the back of the engine (bellhousing, flywheel) and underside (oil pan, starter).
Close-up of the stained/residue area near the mount bracket seen in photo 1.
response.reason: The seller's 'Hyundai Kia 4-cylinder' description covers a wide range of engine displacements and models with very different values, and no engine code, plate, or logo is legible in either photo to narrow this down, so even a worst-case price cannot be anchored without that identifying shot.
